deed: דרו וייסמן ושינוי אבני הבניין של ה-mRNA
title: Drew Weissman and Katalin Karikó changed the building blocks of mRNA, and the coronavirus vaccines relied on this

trailer.text: Drew Weissman, an immunologist and Jewish-American scientist, won the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine together with the Hungarian biochemist Katalin Karikó.
At first, mRNA produced outside the cell caused inflammatory reactions, and enthusiasm for its clinical use was limited.

Weissman and Karikó, colleagues at the University of Pennsylvania, discovered in 2005 that certain modifications of the building blocks of RNA prevent unwanted inflammatory reactions and increase the production of desired proteins.
According to the University of Pennsylvania, the Pfizer/BioNTech and Moderna vaccines against COVID-19 used their technology as a key component.
According to the Nobel Committee, the coronavirus vaccines as a whole, and not only the mRNA vaccines, saved millions of lives and prevented severe disease in many more.

stations.title: Before: a molecule the body rejected

paragraphs.text: Vaccines based on whole viruses, proteins or vectors required large-scale cell culture.
This process limited rapid vaccine production during outbreaks and pandemics.
mRNA had problems of its own.
mRNA produced in vitro was considered unstable and difficult to deliver, so complex lipid systems were needed to encapsulate it.
mRNA produced outside the cell also caused inflammatory reactions.
Because of these obstacles, enthusiasm for mRNA technology for clinical use was initially limited.
According to the Nobel Committee's scientific background, before the coronavirus pandemic no mRNA-based vaccine had been approved for use in humans.
Drew Weissman was born in 1959 in Lexington, Massachusetts, USA.
In 1987 he received MD and PhD degrees in immunology and microbiology from Boston University.
He later joined Anthony Fauci's group at the NIH for a postdoctoral fellowship.
There he studied how HIV interacts with receptors on immune system cells.
A major goal of his was to develop a vaccine against HIV-1, a virus that causes chronic infections.
In 1997 Weissman established his research group at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania.

stations.title: The meeting at the copy machine

paragraphs.text: At the University of Pennsylvania, Weissman met Katalin Karikó and became her new colleague.
According to the Penn website, the two met at a copy machine in the late 1990s.
According to JTA, they discovered that they were working on related topics.

In the early 1990s, when she was an assistant professor at the University of Pennsylvania and before her collaboration with Weissman, Karikó remained true to her vision of developing mRNA as a therapy, despite difficulty convincing funders of the project's importance.
Weissman told Scientific American that Karikó was repeatedly demoted and pushed out.
According to Scientific American, the two continued to search for solutions despite scientific roadblocks, skepticism and funding difficulties.
Weissman said that they saw early on the potential and the importance of RNA, and that this is what kept them going.
Karikó and Weissman noticed that dendritic cells recognize mRNA produced in vitro as a foreign substance.
This recognition activates the cells and releases inflammatory signaling molecules.
When they introduced modifications to the bases of the mRNA, the inflammatory response almost disappeared.
The 2005 study showed that only modifications of uracil (m5U, s2U and ψ) abolished the activation of dendritic cells.
According to Scientific American, the team replaced uridine, one of the building blocks of mRNA, with a similar molecule called pseudouridine.
According to the Committee, this was a paradigm shift in understanding how cells recognize different forms of mRNA.
The results were published in 2005, fifteen years before the coronavirus pandemic.
According to the Committee, the paper received little attention at the time, but laid the foundation for very important developments.
According to Britannica, that same year the two patented nucleoside-modified RNA that does not trigger an immune response.
In studies published in 2008 and 2010, Karikó and Weissman showed that mRNA with base modifications markedly increases protein production.

stations.title: Packaging, a company and a license

paragraphs.text: According to Scientific American, a more efficient delivery system was also developed, with lipid nanoparticles that protect the mRNA and help it enter cells.
Starting in the early 2000s, Karikó and Weissman conducted animal trials of mRNA vaccines against various pathogens, including Zika, influenza and HIV.
In 2006 they founded RNARx to develop new RNA therapies.
According to Britannica, the two licensed the technology to the companies Moderna and BioNTech.
Nobel scientific background: a major improvement in delivery was made in the lab of Pieter Cullis at the University of British Columbia, with ionizable cationic lipids
According to the Penn website, the Pfizer/BioNTech and Moderna vaccines used Karikó and Weissman's technology as a key component.
Weissman said that two months passed from the release of the virus's sequence until the first patients received the vaccine.
Phase 3 trials found high efficacy against symptomatic COVID-19: 95% for the Pfizer/BioNTech vaccine.
According to the Committee, serious adverse effects of the two licensed mRNA vaccines were exceptionally rare.
According to the Committee, the comparison with the Curevac vaccine, which used a lower dose, supports the view that the base modifications were critical for reaching a sufficiently high dose.
The Committee also notes that the comparison is limited, because by the time of the Curevac trial, more neutralization-resistant variants were already circulating.
According to the Committee, there are also approaches to mRNA without modified bases, for example in cancer trials.
According to the Committee, more than 13 billion COVID-19 vaccine doses have been given worldwide, of all vaccine types.
According to the Penn website, the modified mRNA vaccines were given to billions of people worldwide.
According to the Committee, the vaccines saved millions of lives and allowed societies to open and return to normal conditions.
On 2 October 2023 the Nobel Committee announced the award of the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to Karikó and Weissman.
The prize was awarded for discoveries concerning nucleoside base modifications that enabled effective mRNA vaccines against COVID-19.
According to the University of Pennsylvania, representatives of the Nobel Foundation contacted them on the morning of that day.
The prize includes 11 million Swedish crowns, about one million dollars.
According to the 2023 report, the Swedish king was to present the prizes at a ceremony in Stockholm on December 10, 2023.
According to the Penn website, Karikó is one of just 61 women to have won a Nobel Prize, and only the 13th woman to win the Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
Before the Nobel, according to Britannica, the two won the Rosenstiel Award in 2020, and the Louisa Gross Horwitz Prize and the Lasker-DeBakey Award in 2021.
In 2021 Weissman won the Princess of Asturias Award for Scientific Research.
In 2022 the two were elected to the US National Academy of Medicine.
Kathleen Neuzil, a professor of vaccinology, said that the prize is a victory for vaccines and for their potential to advance health and equity.
According to JTA/Forward, Drew Weissman is a Jewish scientist.
He is the son of a Jewish father and a non-Jewish mother, and grew up celebrating Jewish holidays at home, as he told the Philadelphia Jewish Exponent in 2021.
His mother did not convert, but he grew up celebrating all the Jewish holidays.
He told the Exponent that his personal religious outlook is not specifically Jewish.
Weissman and his wife sent their children to Hebrew school at a Conservative synagogue in suburban Philadelphia.
His wife, Mary Ellen, is heavily involved in Momentum, an organization that brings Jewish women closer to Israel, and the couple donated to the organization.
According to the Jinfo website, nearly 40% of US Nobel laureates in medicine have been Jewish.
Weissman receives fan mail from all over the world from people thanking him for his work.
In 2023, at the time of the Nobel Prize announcement, Weissman said he hoped that an mRNA treatment would be available to sickle cell anemia patients within a year and a half.

disagreements.question: When were the first mRNA vaccines against COVID-19 developed or approved?

Britannica: the first mRNA vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 were developed in 2021

claims.quote: Drew Weissman told the Exponent that his personal religious outlook was not specifically Jewish.

claims.text: וייסמן ואשתו שלחו את ילדיהם לבית ספר עברי בבית כנסת קונסרבטיבי בפרוורי פילדלפיה.
claims.quote: he sent his children to Hebrew school at Temple Beth Hillel/Beth El, a Conservative synagogue in suburban Philadelphia.

claims.text: אשתו של וייסמן, מרי אלן, מעורבת מאוד בארגון Momentum שמקרב נשים יהודיות לישראל, והזוג תרם לארגון.
claims.quote: Mary Ellen Weissman is heavily involved in Momentum, which seeks to engage Jewish women with Israel, and together with her husband has spoken to and donated to the organization.

claims.text: לפי אתר Jinfo, כמעט 40% מזוכי נובל האמריקאים ברפואה היו יהודים.
claims.quote: says that nearly 40% of U.S. Nobel laureates in medicine have been Jewish.

claims.text: וייסמן מקווה שטיפול mRNA יהיה זמין לחולי אנמיה חרמשית בעוד שנה וחצי.
claims.quote: Weissman hopes that the mRNA treatment will be available to sickle cell anemia patients in a year and a half.

claims.text: לפי ישראל נשיונל ניוז, וייסמן פגש את קריקו בחנות צילום ב-1997, והשניים שיתפו תסכול על מחסור במימון למחקר RNA למחלות נוירולוגיות.
claims.quote: He met Karikó in a photography shop in 1997, the two shared their frustration over the lack of funding for RNA research for neurological illnesses.

claims.text: לפי הרקע המדעי של נובל, שיפור מרכזי נוסף בהעברה נעשה במעבדתו של פיטר קאליס באוניברסיטת קולומביה הבריטית, עם שומנים קטיוניים ניתנים ליינון.
claims.quote: A second major improvement was made in the lab of Pieter Cullis at the University of British Columbia with the development of ionizable cationic lipids.

claims.text: שני חיסוני mRNA עם בסיסים מותאמים פותחו בקצב שיא; דווחה הגנה של כ-95%, ושניהם אושרו כבר בדצמבר 2020.
claims.quote: Protective effects of around 95% were reported, and both vaccines were approved as early as December 2020.

claims.text: לפי בריטניקה, חיסוני ה-mRNA הראשונים נגד SARS-CoV-2 פותחו ב-2021.
claims.quote: The team’s discoveries enabled the development in 2021 of the first mRNA vaccines, which were targeted against SARS-CoV-2

claims.text: ב-2006 הם הקימו את RNARx כדי לפתח טיפולי RNA חדשים.
claims.quote: The pair founded RNARx, a company focused on developing mRNA therapeutics for a wide range of diseases, in 2006.

claims.text: ב-2021 זכה וייסמן בפרס נסיכת אסטוריאס למחקר מדעי.
claims.quote: with the 2021 Princess of Asturias Award for Technical & Scientific Research, the past 23rd June 2021.

claims.text: אמו לא המירה את דתה, אך הוא גדל בחגיגת כל החגים היהודיים.
claims.quote: While his mother did not convert to Judaism, he said, he grew up celebrating all the Jewish holidays.

claims.text: וייסמן מקבל דואר מעריצים מכל העולם מאנשים שמודים לו על עבודתו.
claims.quote: For months, the postcards and letters have flowed in from across the world,
